title: docs(ci): Dependabot alert triage + disposition decision (65 open alerts)
intent: Adds a read-only triage of the 65 open Dependabot alerts on the default branch, with four disposition options developed for owner ruling. Lands in docs/ci/ beside CI_HYGIENE_DEBT_PATCH_PLAN.md, the analogous artifact that BR-022 cites as its authoritative source. It bumps no dependency, dismisses no alert, and edits no manifest; the ruling is the owner's.
behavior_change: None. Documentation only - adds one new file at its native path. No dependency version, lockfile, package.json, requirements file, workflow, or runtime behaviour is touched.

diff_articulation.what_changed: Adds one new triage document to docs/ci/. It establishes that the 65 alerts are 17 packages (axios alone is 29; axios + vite are 41 of 65); that services/api/requirements.txt - the production Python API that generates G-code - has zero alerts, so nothing here is a machine-safety issue; that 9 alerts including 3 rated high are in dead archived code under archive/** and docs/archive/** that builds nowhere; that the single critical (vitest GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp) requires the Vitest UI server to be listening and no --ui flag appears in any script or workflow, so its precondition is never met; and that axios is browser-only (20 import sites in packages/client/src, none in scripts/ or services/), so its Node-adapter advisories do not execute here while its prototype-pollution, header-injection and cookie-ReDoS advisories do. It identifies BR-021 as a sequencing blocker: client_lint_build.yml:42 and vue_decomposition_gate.yml:31 are continue-on-error, so a vite 5->6 major bump would break the build with CI still green. Four options are developed; Option A (split by risk, clearing 42 of 65 alerts through three low-risk actions) is recommended.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: No dependency-security triage exists anywhere in this repository. Dependency security is currently owned by nothing - no BR-* entry, no CI-RED-* entry, and no SPRINTS.md line - which section 7 records as the durable finding and the reason the alert count reached 65. CI_HYGIENE_DEBT_PATCH_PLAN.md covers CI workflow hygiene (BR-022 / SG_SPEC_TOKEN rollout), not dependency advisories.

commands_run: Alert data pulled live from `gh api repos/HanzoRazer/luthiers-toolbox/dependabot/alerts?state=open&per_page=100` on 2026-08-09 -> 65 open (1 critical / 28 high / 35 medium / 1 low); grouped by severity, manifest, ecosystem, scope, relationship, and package.
Code substrate origin/main @ 0179a032. Direct dependency versions read from packages/client/package.json: axios ^1.13.2, vite ^5.0.0, vitest ^2.1.0, postcss ^8.5.8.
Vitest UI precondition checked: all four client test scripts are plain `vitest run` / `vitest`; `git grep -- --ui` across .github/workflows and packages/client/package.json returned no match.
axios execution context checked: 20 import sites under packages/client/src, zero under scripts/ or services/ - browser-only.
BR-021 gate suppression re-witnessed on origin/main: client_lint_build.yml:42 and vue_decomposition_gate.yml:31 both continue-on-error: true.

files.intent: Triage the 65 open Dependabot alerts by real exposure rather than advisory severity, and develop the disposition options for owner ruling.

architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: Documentation-only addition with no runtime surface. No dependency is bumped and no alert dismissed by this patch. Section 8 states the limits explicitly: the vite 5->6 breaking-change surface was not assessed, so the gated tranche is not authorizable as written, and no exploitability was tested - the triage reasons from advisory preconditions and code-path reachability, which under the defect register's own vocabulary is STATIC-FACT CONFIRMED, not CONFIRMED.
